business_type: mature compounder (system-of-record SaaS under an agentic-disruption narrative)
moat_source: CRM system-of-record status, data gravity (Data 360), and enterprise process embedding; evidence: +52% EPS growth and $6.6B quarterly FCF while the market prices decline - customer data does not migrate on a narrative

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% closed by year 3. Scenario FCF is SBC-adjusted (~3.3B/yr haircut from historical norms). The $25B buyback (retiring ~4-5%/yr at this price) is NOT modeled and adds materially to all scenarios.

sensitivity_key_driver: seat retention through the agentic transition (net revenue retention)
primary_model_risk: Same as ADBE: the bear case (agents shrink seats faster than Agentforce/Data 360 revenue replaces them, FCF eroding from 2028) is genuinely live and carries 30% weight. Salesforce's five-acquisitions-a-year habit adds a second, self-inflicted risk ADBE lacks: capital allocation could burn the discount before the narrative resolves.
expectations_gap_key_variable: seat economics: at ~12-14x forward earnings the price implies stagnation-to-decline; reported growth is +10-11% guided with Agentforce compounding at +205% - the market is paying for the bear case while the filings print the base case
top_5_bull_arguments: Second 'market too pessimistic' verdict of the run: ~10x FCF for the CRM system of record with +52% EPS growth
Agentforce $1.2B ARR at +205% is the fastest new-product ramp in company history - the disruptor revenue is landing INSIDE Salesforce
$25B buyback at a three-year-low price is exactly when buybacks create value
FY27 guide (+10-11%) with H2 re-acceleration gives a near-term falsifiable bull checkpoint
Data gravity: agents need the customer data Salesforce already hosts - the moat may transfer to the agent era rather than dissolve
top_5_bear_arguments: Seat cannibalization is unfalsified: if agents cut human seats 20-30%, per-seat pricing cannot be replaced fast enough
Five acquisitions in 2026 - every one dropped the stock; capital-allocation grade C is earned
Agentforce's +205% is off a base that is ~2.6% of total revenue - it cannot carry the P&L for years
Analyst fair values still being cut (Simply Wall St 317 to 255; RBC/BofA cautious) - the falling-knife phase may not be over
SBC (~3.3B/yr) consumes a third of the buyback before any share-count reduction happens
thesis_breakers: Net revenue retention below 100% (seat erosion confirmed)
Agentforce ARR growth below 80% y/y (the replacement engine stalling)
A sixth major acquisition in 2026 (capital discipline broken)
Operating cash flow growth turning negative y/y
position_size_recommendation: 2-3%; second-best risk/reward found after ADBE - the same disruption-fear discount on a wide moat, with the acquisition habit as the differentiating (and sizing-limiting) flaw
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios. EPS/FCF/guidance/Agentforce ARR are reported; the FY27 FCF level is inferred from guided OCF growth (Q1's 6.6B is seasonally front-loaded) and SBC is estimated from historical norms - confidence_level medium.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence. Verified datapoints: stock -30% YTD 2026, -45% from highs, three-year low (coverage); trailing P/E 19.28 vs forward 11.92-14.2; +9.41% past week (pass1). MacroTrends historical P/E series exists but no specific range was captured.
